The fixture feeds the same top-level mip data and CLUT sizes as the production callbacks, the renderer's 270-page NTSC cache capacity, 127 CLUT slots, and the 1.5 MiB per-frame upload budget. It scans all resources for two consecutive frame numbers and records uploads, hits, deferrals, and occupied-page high-water.

All maps completed both scans with zero TC_FULL failures, owner and scratch bounds intact, outer canaries intact, and cache flush/owner rewind verified. Blood Gulch is the closest RAM owner at 3,954,720 / 4,014,928 bytes (60,208 bytes free). Sidewinder is 3,697,632 bytes. Blood Gulch's conservative all-resource pass deferred two uploads in frame 0; frame 1 accepted those two, with the other 76 resources as cache hits. Thus the candidate is tight but this resource set did not reveal an intrinsically uncacheable texture or permanent upload-budget starvation.

owner is the high-water of co-resident converted section data in the candidate render owner. cache high-water is occupied texture pages under the actual renderer cache API; the 270-page limit reflects the current 512x448 NTSC mode and renderer's reserved pages, as derived below. uploads / hits / deferred list frame 0 then frame 1.

The runtime emits one row per map with scratch high-water 98,304 / 524,288 bytes. Selected MODL coverage ranged from 4 models / 23 parts on Putput to 25 models / 163 parts on Blood Gulch; these are converter model-section counts, not spawned-object counts.

- The production world.c:21-37 callback supplies mip 0, its pixel bytes, and the CLUT; world.c:43-57 supplies lightmap page pixels and the shared 1,024-byte CLUT. This fixture uses those same parser views.

- submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/render/bsp_render.c:29-33 reserves 16 texture-window pages for CLUTs and one for the font. Its pages_for and resident_tex0 at :344-382 compute page occupancy, charge pixel-plus-CLUT upload bytes, request a cache entry, and enqueue the real GS upload pair. :800-802 and :832-840 establish texture/lightmap/object key ordering and the 1.5 MiB budget.

- The page count used by the diagnostic follows platform/video.h (512x448, 4 MiB GS VRAM) and platform/video.c:14-29: the two CT16 framebuffers and Z24 buffer consume 1,835,008 bytes (224 GS pages), and bsp_render.c:164 starts the texture window after the extra allocated page. 512 total GS pages - 224 framebuffer/Z pages - 1 window-base page - 17 CLUT/font pages = 270 cache pages.

- Halo-64's `submodules/halo-64/port/n64/NOTES.md:115-155` is a useful comparison for why its texture policy cannot be copied: its first-person atlas had to be split into windows and represented as small CI4 textures, while it also describes tradeoffs around its level texture path. This measurement instead uses this repository's halo-ps2 GS/VRAM/cache implementation and its 270-page renderer window; no N64 texture or pool limit is imported.

The current parent binds the whole dynamic arena to the compatibility allocator, so it is not an unused secondary object pool ([hcu_memory_bind.c:60](../../src/stream/hcu_memory_bind.c#L60)). The allocator is a bounded bump store whose `free` does not reclaim individual allocations ([ps2_memory.c:300](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/ps2/src/ps2_memory.c#L300)). Carving a typed object store from it must reduce the compatibility span by precisely the same amount and prove all remaining compatibility allocations fit; the two cannot both own the same bytes.

The validator implements exact byte-set membership. `claim()` rejects any overlap and otherwise marks bytes, including a prefix before it detects a later overlap; its aligned-word branch checks all 32 bytes before claiming any byte in that word, which limits the failure prefix. `unclaim()` clears a range ([tag_validate.c:477](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/linux/game/tag_validate.c#L477)). `tag_validate_any_claimed()` is also used by the model-index validator ([tag_schema_models.c:443](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/linux/game/tag_schema_models.c#L443)). An exact sorted disjoint interval representation is a valid candidate: retain half-open byte ranges with adjacent ranges merged; query via binary search; split/remove intervals when clearing the BSP domain. Each interval needs at least two 32-bit offsets, eight bytes total, plus metadata and update workspace. A record-count bound and a checked capacity failure are mandatory. Arbitrary malformed input can alternate occupied/unoccupied bytes, so the worst-case interval representation can be larger than the bitmap. It must fail atomically and safely if its bounded table fills, and the required retail corpus must demonstrate a sufficient bound. Four-byte-granularity bitmaps are not equivalent because names and opaque data may occupy unaligned bytes.

verbatim_lines.raw: The PS2 production transition order is unsafe for a singleton CTAG-backed map owner. **CE `game_dispose_from_old_map()` must run before `game_unload()` when an old scenario is loaded.** On this port, `game_unload()` calls `scenario_unload()`, and the PS2 `scenario_unload()` path first clears the CE scenario/BSP globals and then calls `ps2_cache_release_map_owner()`. The parent callback unloads the CTAG mount/source and makes the old tag/BSP storage available for reuse. Calling CE disposal only afterward reverses the lifetime contract: old-map callbacks execute after the storage and global pointers they are meant to retire have been unpublished/released.
1. CE’s `game_unload()` only calls `scenario_unload()` when `game_globals->map_loaded` is true ([`game.c:754-785`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L754)).

2. CE’s `game_dispose_from_old_map()` performs map-derived cleanup—including structures, render objects, objects, players, effects, sound, and scenario cleanup—and calls `scenario_dispose_from_old_map()` near the end ([`game.c:946-984`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L946)).

3. `scenario_unload()` calls `scenario_tags_unload()`, clears `global_scenario`, `global_structure_bsp`, `global_collision_bsp`, `global_bsp3d`, and `global_game_globals`, then releases the PS2 parent map owner ([`scenario.c:387-425`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/scenario/scenario.c#L387)). `scenario_tags_unload()` closes tag consumers and clears the cache header/tag table publication before returning ([`cache_files.c:617-658`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/cache/cache_files.c#L617)).

6. Retail CE control flow independently corroborates disposal-before-unload: non-PS2 map transition code calls `game_dispose_from_old_map()` before `game_unload()` ([`main.c:1612-1621`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L1612), [`main.c:1984-1988`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L1984), and [`network_game_manager.c:801-805`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/networking/network_game_manager.c#L801)). The PS2-specific early-unload branches are the divergence.

The strongest concrete consequence is a dangling/invalid old-map lifetime at subsequent disposers. For example, `game_dispose_from_old_map()` calls `objects_dispose_from_old_map()` before `scenario_dispose_from_old_map()` ([`game.c:965-980`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/game/game.c#L965)); object teardown walks and frees map-era object datums and invalidates cluster partitions ([`objects.c:1172-1205`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c#L1172)). The sequence is designed as an ordered CE teardown, not as a harmless second idempotent clear after scenario unload. Not every individual callback has been proven to dereference a tag byte on every map, so the exact failure mechanism for a particular run is an inference; the ownership/lifetime violation itself is directly proven.
| Site | Classification | Present PS2 sequence | Audit disposition |

| `source/main/main.c:1612-1622`, `main_change_map_name()` | Production local map replacement | preflight → `game_unload()` → `game_dispose_from_old_map()` → precache successor → new map | **Fix required.** Keep preflight before mutation; reverse only the teardown pair to dispose old state while its tag owner is live, then unload/release it before successor materialization. Add a `port:` comment that states this ownership ordering. |

| `source/main/main.c:1974-1978`, `main_load_ui_scenario()` PS2 block | Production return-to-menu/UI map replacement | preflight UI → unload old map → dispose old state → precache UI | **Fix required.** Preserve preflight-before-teardown, then dispose-before-unload. This covers return from gameplay/co-op to UI. |

| `source/main/main.c:2912-2926`, `main_setup_connection()` PS2 local startup | Production initial/local-session map setup | preflight → unload → dispose → precache → `main_new_map()` | **Fix required when an old scenario/map is present** (e.g. an already loaded UI or reused local-session state). Even if cold boot normally has no loaded map, retain one safe order and document the conditional lifecycle contract rather than relying on an empty-map assumption. |

| `source/main/main.c:1524-1552`, `hcu_step8_test_start_local_map()` | Test-only entry used to start the Step 8 local workload | preflight → unload → dispose → precache | **Fix required for fixture fidelity.** This is the route that transitions the startup UI into the workload map; currently it contradicts `step8_workload_cleanup()` and can itself reproduce the order bug. Mark the test-only code with `port:`/diagnostic scope and test the real sequence after correction. |

| `source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c:64-72`, capacity-diagnostic initial UI release | Test-only | menu unload → game unload → dispose | **Fix required for diagnostic fidelity** when UI scenario is loaded. `main_menu_unload()` only clears shell/music flags ([`main.c:1130-1137`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/main/main.c#L1130)); it does not retire the scenario/tag owner. |

| `source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c:336-348`, post-preflight-fault setup | Test-only M2 UI lifecycle diagnostic | menu unload → game unload → dispose → retry UI | **Fix required for diagnostic fidelity.** It disposes the old UI only after its tag owner has been released; this undermines the lifecycle regression’s ownership premise even if its assertions happen to pass on a given build. |

| `source/main/ps2_m2_ui_lifecycle_test.c:289-296`, Step 8 workload cleanup | Test-only | dispose → unload | **Correct ordering; retain.** This is the source-backed invariant the other test-only teardown paths should match. |

| `source/main/main.c:2944-2955`, `main_reset_map_private()` | Production in-map BSP reset, not full map unload | switch BSP → dispose old-map transient state → reinitialize | **Do not blindly add `game_unload()`.** This does not release the full map owner; it is an in-place BSP/game reset. Keep it as a separate transition class and regression-check that no new full-owner release is introduced. |

| `source/main/main.c:2486-2487`, `main_exit()` | Process/game shutdown | dispose old-map → full game dispose; no `game_unload()` in this function | **Not the defective pair.** Verify outer shutdown has stopped map processing before global disposal, but do not treat this as a map replacement call site. |

| `source/networking/network_game_manager.c:801-805` | CE multiplayer map entry | dispose → unload | **Already correct in source.** Confirm the relevant PS2 local/network build actually includes this call path before adding any duplicate cleanup. |

The PS2 branches needing production source-marked ordering edits are therefore three `main.c` paths (map-name transition, return-to-UI, local startup) plus the test-only Step 8 start helper. Two diagnostic-only paths need order correction to avoid tests normalizing the bug. The network manager and in-map BSP reset are controls, not fixes.

Use one exact image and record ELF/source pins. verbatim_lines.raw: This audit expands the prior static BSP/scenario texture inventory to the gameplay content a multiplayer match can select. It is strictly the 13 named Halo CE multiplayer maps; campaign maps are not inputs. The audited maps are Beaver Creek, Blood Gulch, Boarding Action, Carousel, Chill Out, Damnation, Hang 'Em High, Longest, Prisoner, Putput, Rat Race, Sidewinder, and Wizard. Their current decompressed files' hashes match the earlier “retail map” inventory. The prior reports identify their extraction source as XISO SHA-256 `43ec0813edadd592b7b489a930f108d289db9313ac337611110ffca8be0a7258`, but that original XISO is not currently in `build/`; this pass verifies the extracted map bytes, not a fresh extraction from that XISO.

Across the 13 alternative maps, the unique path union contains 1,767 tag paths and the summed per-map tag-union count is 53,207,883 bytes. That sum is a catalog total, not a concurrent allocation. Blood Gulch is largest for the walked in-image tag union (4,260,147 bytes), MODL output (4,563,904), OTEX output (3,027,136), and combined static-TEXS/LM plus full-closure OTEX output (3,466,272). The latter is below the nominal 4,194,304-byte `texture_cache` reservation in [`config/memory-budget.json`](../../config/memory-budget.json#L13), but is not proof that those sections are actually owned by or resident in that arena.

The schema walk also records 894–897 `file_data` descriptors/map, with declared byte totals of 11,016,000–11,460,456 across the walked records. Reachable bitmap tags refer to 16,409,600–19,622,400 unique source pixel-interval bytes/map in the decompressed map inputs (Blood Gulch is 19,622,400). These are *input/source extents*, not a recommendation to retain raw bitmap pixels on EE RAM; the conversion pipeline moves selected render data to converted packs. The complete per-map breakdown and source flags are in the JSON. The raw in-image tag union alone is below the 6,815,744-byte `resident_gameplay` reservation, but is not the converted CTAG image size or a resident high-water result; relocation/compaction, stripped graphics fields, file-data ownership, CE global data, and allocator metadata still determine actual fit.

1. Scenario-selected object assets materially undercount a match's content. For Beaver Creek the prior selected object set was 12 models, 875,808-byte OTEX, and 371,248-byte ANIM; the closure contains 53 models, 2,759,776-byte OTEX, and 652,160-byte ANIM. Across maps, full closure OTEX is 2,273,344–3,027,136 bytes versus scenario-only OTEX 389,376–1,705,504 bytes in the companion inventory. The full closure adds 38–41 model tags and 14–17 animation-graph tags over the scenario/sky baseline, depending on the map.

3. Every audited retail MP map has 15 weapon tags, 14 equipment tags, 2 biped tags, 3 vehicle tags, and 16 projectile tags. The source-map name scan finds the Gravity Rifle in all 13 maps, but no Energy Sword or Fuel Rod tag in any of them. **The two requested custom weapons cannot be covered by this stock retail-MP closure:** their tag roots, models, FP models/animation, projectile/effect dependencies (Fuel Rod), converted assets, and runtime residency need a separately provisioned mod/port asset source and must be added to the acceptance closure. This is an asset-source gap, not an inference that those weapons cannot be implemented.

5. Dynamic gameplay pool constraints are a separate measurement. The pinned CE PS2 limits retain source/Xbox capacities, not accepted EE byte allocations: e.g. 2,048 object slots and a 1 MiB object pool are declared in [`halo_ps2_limits.h`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/port/ps2/include/halo_ps2_limits.h#L30), object initialization allocates the object data array and object memory pool ([`objects.c`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/objects/objects.c#L1039)), AI uses a 256-actor array ([`actors.c`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/ai/actors.c#L564)), and particles allocate 1,024 × 0x70-byte data entries ([`particles.c`](../../submodules/halo-ce-universal/source/effects/particles.c#L230)). These allocations are routed via CE `game_state_data_new`/memory-pool ownership and cannot be equated with measured occupancy of the 2,621,440-byte `dynamic_simulation` reservation. A multiplayer acceptance fixture must measure actual allocations and high-water under maximum supported players/bots, vehicles, projectiles, effects, and simultaneous ordnance.

Step 8 must establish the actual caller/arena and measure retained bytes plus temporary source/decode overlap.

- The biggest measured pack-section subtotal here (TEXS + LM + full OTEX) is 3,466,272 bytes, but it does not establish cache fit: decoded source copies, GS upload staging, texture deduplication policy, fragmentation, simultaneous map transition, renderer pins, and arena routing are outside this offline conversion result. verbatim_lines.raw: # M2 Step 8: static render-asset inventory for 13 stock multiplayer maps

I generated a reproducible, per-map inventory of converted BSP textures (`TEXS`), all converted lightmap sections (`LMn`), and scenario-selected object textures (`OTEX`) for the complete 13-map stock multiplayer set. This addresses the *offline static converted-section size* subquestion in Step 8; it is not a runtime cache high-water measurement, map-admission proof, or all-render-state bound.

The largest converted static texture-section sum is Blood Gulch at **2,144,640 bytes** (2.045 MiB); Sidewinder is next at 1,838,656 bytes. All 13 maps together sum to 14,880,288 bytes, but that is an *across-alternatives catalog total* and must not be charged as simultaneous live memory. Each row is the sum of one map's `TEXS` + scenario-selected `OTEX` + all its converted `LMn` sections. These rows do not include BSP geometry, object MODL/SCEN/ANIM/SKY sections, runtime-created effects, weapons, UI, DMA staging, decoded Xbox source buffers, cache fragmentation, or transition overlap.

The measured largest row is below the configured 4,194,304-byte `texture_cache` reservation in [`config/memory-budget.json`](../../config/memory-budget.json#L13), but this is not proof that those bytes are allocated from that reservation today. The parent/halo-ps2 section loader takes a caller-supplied arena and copies section payloads there; `world_load()` retains BSP, TEXS, and the selected LM section in its `arena` argument, and `world_load_objects()` retains MODL/SCEN and optional OTEX in its supplied arena ([`world.c`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/world.c#L58), [`world.c`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/world.c#L103), [`section.c`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/section.c#L153)). Therefore the sums are asset sizes that an ownership design must place, not evidence that the current 4 MiB reservation is the allocator backing them or that concurrent live working set fits. The renderer consumes TEXS/LM payloads as source views ([`world.c`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/world.c#L5), [`tex.c`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/engine/src/world/tex.c#L24)); these data are not evidence of a measured residency/eviction policy.

The isolated audit is [`tools/audit_mp_render_asset_bound.py`](../../tools/audit_mp_render_asset_bound.py#L1). It hard-requires the 13 stock MP map filenames (campaign files are not included), runs pinned halo-ps2 `texconv.convert_map(..., lightmaps=True, lm_gain=1.5)`, parses the emitted `TEXS` and every `LMn`, and runs `scenconv.collect()` plus `modelconv.convert_map()` on the scenario-selected model tags and sky model. Its method corresponds to [`texconv.py`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/tools/halo2ps2/texconv.py#L973), which filters shader textures to BSP material references and lightmap pages referenced by rendered materials, and [`modelconv.py`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/tools/halo2ps2/modelconv.py#L829), which converts the supplied set of model tags and builds their OTEX. This is a deterministic conversion inventory, not a count of all bitmap tags in an Xbox map and not an all-gameplay-object closure.

The audit JSON stores every raw decompressed map SHA-256, each per-map `TEXS`/`OTEX`/`LMn` section SHA-256, count/byte subtotals, converter identity, and source pin. Two full conversions completed with byte-identical JSON (`static-render-assets-v2.json` and `static-render-assets-v3.json`, each 29,098 bytes). Both JSON files report the source directory `build/retail-maps/decompressed`, halo-ps2 pin `71183bb0a9adc586cd267b2780c82bbc12cfd95b`, HCU pin `6933490b2d16bb1c637295b6a0f3880ba23a7d56`, and audit-script SHA-256 `466210ce16d208803020c144750c5b0cfb4a81dd8ff0f694da5f103e716b751a`. The v2/v3 JSON SHA-256 is `fae6288e6335ab6f0afa41bb61074e49046aa823ff8d0cc740f9f815c6e1904f` (identical outputs). Per-source map hashes and output-section hashes are inside that JSON.

- `LMn` conversion honors the converter's 512 KiB per-BSP pixel guard and configured extra shrink behavior ([`texconv.py`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/tools/halo2ps2/texconv.py#L63), [`texconv.py`](../../submodules/halo-ps2/tools/halo2ps2/texconv.py#L973)). The observed *sum of each map's selected LMAP sections* is only 16,288–113,440 bytes; this does not include temporary full-resolution decode buffers or demonstrate PS2 EE placement.

- The 14,880,288-byte all-map total is not a simultaneously resident demand and cannot be compared as a single-map allocation. Do not use it to justify taking 170,176 bytes from texture cache, and do not use the per-map max alone to accept such a transfer.

This closes only the reproducible offline static asset-size inventory subcheck. Step 8 remains open for physical arena ownership/high-water, map transition overlap, scenario and match-time object closure, bot/co-op runtime load, EE/PCSX2 rendering, and acceptance across all 13 maps.
